newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali faction leader warns foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Somali faction leader warns foreigners.

text.p: Somali faction leader Hussein Aideed has warned foreign aid workers and journalists that they risked punishment if they visited the country without permission from his administration, his radio said on Thursday.
The radio, quoting Aideed in an end of year address to the battered Horn of Africa nation, said he had information that foreigners were entering Somalia without going through his immigration system.

The self-styled president, whose authority lies only in the southern part of the divided capital, said "any foreigner found to be staying in Mogadishu without having legal residence permit will face severe punishment".

The younger Aideed took over control of south Mogadishu last year after the death of his father Mohamed Farah Aideed, a ruthless general who humbled U.S. forces in Somalia. The son immediately proclaimed himself president of Somalia -- a move opposed by rival factions headed by north Mogadishu leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed.
In his address, Aideed said his government achieved progress during 1996 in the areas of tax collection, reconciliation among various clans and disarmament.
Aideed dedicated 1997 to the restoration of public services which collapsed during the war.

Somalia has been without a central administration since 1991 after rebels overthrew the late president Mohamed Siad Barre. But they soon turned their guns on each other in murderous battles that laid waste to Somalia and sparked a famine.
